security_audit.summary: The static external command and network alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline Java identifiers, and Azure endpoint examples. One semantic issue was found: the token access example demonstrates partial access-token logging, which can leak sensitive credential material if copied.

remediation.issue: The token access example prints part of an access token.
remediation.suggestion: Remove token value logging entirely. Show only expiration metadata, refresh status, or a fixed placeholder that cannot reveal credential material.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Token Logging Example
semantic_findings.description: The token access example warns not to expose tokens, but then prints the first 20 characters of a token. Developers may copy this pattern into logs and expose credential material.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited Java example directly prints a substring of token.getToken(), which is sensitive even when partially redacted. The surrounding warning reduces intent risk, but the example remains unsafe.

content.value_statement: Java developers often need clear patterns for Azure Communication Services credentials and identifiers. This skill provides focused examples for tokens, refresh, identity types, and cloud environments.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Maven dependency for azure-communication-common.
Explains CommunicationTokenCredential creation with static tokens and refresh options.
Demonstrates identifier types for ACS users, phone numbers, Teams users, and unknown IDs.
Covers Entra Communication token credential options and Teams scopes.
Lists cloud environment constants and common environment variable names.
limitations: Does not provide a complete runnable Java project.
Does not create or manage Azure resources.
Does not validate real tokens, tenants, or service endpoints.
Examples require adaptation and security review before production use.

use_cases.title: Add ACS Chat Authentication
use_cases.description: Use the credential examples to connect an existing Java chat client with Azure Communication Services authentication.

use_cases.title: Plan Token Refresh Behavior
use_cases.description: Compare static tokens, proactive refresh, and asynchronous refresh patterns for a long-running client.

use_cases.title: Normalize Communication Identifiers
use_cases.description: Map raw ACS, phone, Teams, and unknown identifiers into typed Java objects for safer processing.

prompt_templates.title: Explain The Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how CommunicationTokenCredential works in Azure Communication Services Java. Include when to use static tokens and refresh options.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Identifier Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the right Azure Communication Services Java identifier types for ACS users, phone numbers, Teams users, and unknown IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Token Refresh Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Java token refresh flow for Azure Communication Services. Check lifecycle handling, refresh timing, and sensitive logging risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Environment Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ACS Java authentication approach for public, government, and Teams Phone Extensibility scenarios using credential and cloud environment options.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to create an ACS chat client with token refresh.
output_examples.output: The response outlines dependency setup, credential construction, proactive refresh, client builder wiring, and a warning to avoid token logging.

output_examples.input: A backend engineer asks how to parse mixed communication identifiers.
output_examples.output: The response maps ACS users, phone numbers, Teams users, and unknown values to the correct Java identifier classes.

output_examples.input: A team asks how Entra authentication fits Teams Phone Extensibility.
output_examples.output: The response explains the browser credential inputs, resource endpoint, required scope, and where tenant-specific validation is needed.

best_practices: Use proactive token refresh for long-lived Java clients.
Keep tokens out of logs, traces, screenshots, and support tickets.
Use typed communication identifiers instead of raw strings when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not print access tokens or token substrings during debugging.
Do not hardcode tenant, resource, or user values in reusable code.
Do not treat unknown identifiers as trusted users without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill install the Azure SDK?
faq.answer: No. It shows the Maven dependency and usage patterns for the Java package.

faq.question: Can it create Azure Communication Services resources?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Java common types, credentials, token refresh, and identifiers.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is the token refresh code production ready?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as a pattern and adapt it with secure storage, error handling, and monitoring.

faq.question: What Azure services does it relate to?
faq.answer: It relates to Azure Communication Services clients such as chat, calling, and Teams Phone Extensibility.

faq.question: Does it handle every identifier type?
faq.answer: No. It covers common ACS, phone, Teams, and unknown identifier examples.
